SOURCE: "Slot-Gated Modeling for Joint Slot Filling and Intent Prediction", Chih-Wen Goo, Guang Gao, Yun-Kai Hsu, Chih-Li Huo, Tsung-Chieh Chen, Keng-Wei Hsu, Yun-Nung Chen (National Taiwan University; Institute for Information Industry). Proceedings of NAACL-HLT 2018, pages 753–757. The PDF does not print a DOI.

COVERAGE: I read all 5 pages (pp. 753–757) in full, including the abstract, method, setup, Tables 1–3, results, conclusion and references. I skipped nothing. The PDF prints no arXiv id for this paper. The only arXiv id in it belongs to a reference: Bahdanau et al. 2014, "arXiv:1409.0473".

File: /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/generative-ai/07-agentic-applications/sources/goo-2018-slot-gated-modeling-joint-slot.pdf

CLAIMS
- claim: The slot-gated model (full attention) improves sentence-level semantic frame accuracy over the Liu & Lane (2016) attention model by about 4.2% relative on ATIS and 1.9% relative on Snips.
  number: 4.2% (ATIS), 1.9% (Snips), relative
  setup: The comparison is against the Atten.-Based baseline (Liu and Lane, 2016). Hidden size 64, Adam, results averaged over 20 runs. Check: 82.2/78.9 = +4.2%, 75.5/74.1 = +1.9%.
  quote: "significantly improves sentence-level semantic frame accuracy with 4.2% and 1.9% relative improvement compared to the attentional model on benchmark ATIS and Snips datasets respectively"
  where: p.753 (p1), abstract. Section 3.2 on p.756 gives the ATIS figure as "around 4.1% and 1.9%". The two statements disagree slightly (see PROBLEMS).
- claim: Full results table (Table 3, %), in the order slot F1 / intent accuracy / sentence accuracy for ATIS, then the same for Snips.
  number: as quoted
  setup: Test sets are ATIS (893 utterances) and Snips (700 utterances). † marks a significant improvement over all baselines (p<0.05, one-tailed t-test).
  quote: "Joint Seq. (Hakkani-T¨ur et al., 2016) 94.3 92.6 80.7 87.3 96.9 73.2 / Atten.-Based (Liu and Lane, 2016) 94.2 91.1 78.9 87.8 96.7 74.1 / Proposed Slot-Gated (Full Atten.) 94.8† 93.6† 82.2† 88.8† 97.0 75.5† / Slot-Gated (Intent Atten.) 95.2† 94.1† 82.6† 88.3 96.8 74.6"
  where: p.756 (p4), Table 3
- claim: Absolute gains of full attention over Liu & Lane are, on ATIS, +0.6 slot F1, +2.5 intent accuracy and +3.3 sentence accuracy. On Snips they are +1.0 slot F1, +0.3 intent accuracy (not significant) and +1.4 sentence accuracy. The gains are largest at sentence level.
  number: derived from Table 3 (my own arithmetic, not stated by the authors)
  setup: Same as above.
  quote: "It is obvious that our proposed model performs better especially on sentence-level semantic frame results, where the relative improvement is around 4.1% and 1.9% for ATIS and Snips respectively."
  where: p.756
- claim: The intent-attention-only variant is slightly better on ATIS with fewer parameters, but it does not beat full attention on Snips. The authors explain this by task complexity.
  number: 284K to 251K parameters
  setup: ATIS vs Snips
  quote: "In ATIS dataset, the proposed slot-gated model with only intent attention achieves slightly better performance with fewer parameters (from 284K to 251K). However, it does not achieve better results in Snips dataset."
  where: p.756
- claim: The core idea is that slots depend on intent. Earlier joint models shared only a loss function, so they modelled the slot-intent link "implicitly". The slot gate models it "explicitly" by conditioning slot prediction on the intent context vector.
  number: none
  setup: BLSTM encoder with attention
  quote: "the prior work did not “explicitly” model the relationships between the intent and slots; instead, it applied a joint loss function to “implicitly” consider both cues."
  where: p.753
- claim: The gate is g = Σ v·tanh(c^S_i + W·c^I), and it scales the slot context: y^S_i = softmax(W^S_hy(h_i + c^S_i·g)). A larger g means slot attention and intent attention focus on the same part of the input.
  number: none
  setup: Eqs. 6–7
  quote: "A larger g indicates that the slot context vector and the intent context vector pay attention to the same part of the input sequence, which also infers that the correlation between the slot and the intent is stronger"
  where: p.755
- claim: The joint objective factorises as p(y^I|x) multiplied by the product over t of p(y^S_t|x), and is maximised over both tasks together.
  number: none
  setup: Eq. 10
  quote: "p(yS,y I| x) is the conditional probability of the understanding result (slot filling and intent prediction) given the input word sequence and is maximized for SLU."
  where: p.755
- claim: Joint models are motivated by error propagation in pipelined approaches.
  number: none
  setup: general
  quote: "Considering that pipelined approaches usually suffer from error propagation due to their independent models, the joint model for slot filling and intent detection has been proposed to improve sentence-level semantics"
  where: p.753
- claim: Dataset statistics (Table 1). ATIS has a vocabulary of 722, 120 slots, 21 intents and 4,478/500/893 train/dev/test utterances. Snips has a vocabulary of 11,241, 72 slots, 7 intents and 13,084/700/700. ATIS intents are highly imbalanced.
  number: 74%
  setup: ATIS training data
  quote: "intents in ATIS are highly unbalanced, where atis flight accounts for about 74% of training data while atis cheapest appears only once."
  where: p.755–756
- claim: Training setup.
  number: hidden size 64, 20 runs, 10/20 epochs
  setup: all experiments
  quote: "we set the size of hidden vectors to 64, the optimizer is adam, the reported numbers are averaged over 20 runs, and the maximum epoch is set to 10 and 20 on ATIS and Snips respectively with an early-stop strategy."
  where: p.756
- claim: Metrics. Slot filling uses F1, intent detection uses accuracy, and semantic frame parsing uses whole-frame (sentence) accuracy.
  number: none
  quote: "slot filling using F1 score, intent prediction using accuracy, and sentence-level semantic frame parsing using whole frame accuracy."
  where: p.756

LIMITS:
- Evaluation covers only two small benchmarks, ATIS (single domain, airline) and Snips (7 intents). Each utterance has exactly one intent. Inputs are text transcripts.
- Only two baselines are compared, both from 2016. The model has no CRF layer and no pretrained embeddings or pretrained language models. This 2018 BLSTM work predates BERT-era joint models, so the numbers are dated as state of the art.
- The improvements are small in absolute terms (0.6–3.3 points). On Snips the intent accuracy gain (96.7 to 97.0) is not marked significant, and the intent-attention variant's Snips gains are not significant either.
- The authors concede the gate helps more on simple tasks: "the slot-gated model is more useful for a simple understanding task, because the slot-intent relations are stronger and easily modeled" (p.757).
- The introduction promises gate-based analysis of slot-intent relations ("the gating results help us analyze the slot-intent relations"), but the paper never shows one.
- There are no error analysis, ablations beyond the two variants, or confidence intervals. Results are averages over 20 runs with no variance reported.

BUILDS ON: Liu and Lane (2016), the attention-based RNN joint model and the direct baseline. Hakkani-Tür et al. (2016), the multi-domain joint BLSTM. Guo et al. (2014) and Chen et al. (2016), earlier joint models. Bahdanau et al. (2014), attention. Mesnil et al. (2015), the BLSTM for slot filling. Liu and Lane (2015). The task framing follows Tur and De Mori (2011). Earlier slot-filling methods cited: Raymond and Riccardi (2007) for CRF and Yao et al. (2014) for LSTM. The ATIS citation is Tur et al. (2010).

CODE: The paper prints no code. It links a repository (p.753, footnote 1): "The code is available at: https://github.com/MiuLab/SlotGated-SLU." The Snips data is at https://github.com/snipsco/nlu-benchmark/tree/master/2017-06-custom-intent-engines (p.755, footnote 2).

FIGURES:
- Figure 1, p.1 (753): "An example utterance with annotations of semantic slots in IOB format (S) and intent (I), B-dir and I-dir denote the director name." Best candidate for the note. "find comedies by james cameron" is labelled O B-genre O B-dir I-dir with intent find_movie, so one line shows what intent detection and slot filling each produce. It is simple enough to reproduce as a text table.
- Figure 2, p.2 (754): "The architecture of the proposed slot-gated models." This shows the full-attention and intent-only-attention variants. It is useful only if the note covers architecture.
- Figure 3, p.3 (755): "Illustration of the slot gate." This is a small diagram of the gate.

PROBLEMS:
- The relative improvement on ATIS is stated two ways: "4.2%" in the abstract (p.753) and "around 4.1%" in Section 3.2 (p.756). The Table 3 numbers (82.2 vs 78.9) give 4.2%.
- The text on p.756 says significance is shown with "star markers", but Table 3 uses the † symbol.
- Extraction is otherwise clean. There are minor ligature and diacritic artefacts ("Hakkani-T¨ur", "Beyonc"), and the "atis_flight" underscores were lost.
- The text contains no embedded instructions.
